# Define and load a workflow

<!-- description: The loaders that read a workflow into a WorkflowDefinition, and the types of the definition they return. -->

<!-- Generated by scripts/generate-library-reference.mjs from the API reports and the built declarations; do not edit by hand: after `npm run build`, run `npm run docs:library`. -->

`loadWorkflowFromFile` and `loadWorkflowFromString` read a workflow and return its `WorkflowDefinition`; their `…WithDiagnostics` forms also return the loader's warnings and the paths it could not check. This page lists the loaders, the error codes Realm raises, and the definition's types; what each field of the workflow file means is on the workflow reference pages.

Where the docs teach it: [Workflow file: top-level fields](../workflow/top-level-fields.md), [Core library: run a workflow from your own program](../core-library.md#run-a-workflow-from-your-own-program).

| Name | Kind | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`loadWorkflowFromFile`](#loadworkflowfromfile) | function | Loads a WorkflowDefinition from a YAML file on disk. |
| [`loadWorkflowFromFileWithDiagnostics`](#loadworkflowfromfilewithdiagnostics) | function | Same as `loadWorkflowFromFile`, but prints nothing and returns every collected LoaderWarning alongside the definition (issue #169). |
| [`loadWorkflowFromString`](#loadworkflowfromstring) | function | Loads a WorkflowDefinition from a YAML string. |
| [`loadWorkflowFromStringWithDiagnostics`](#loadworkflowfromstringwithdiagnostics) | function | Same as `loadWorkflowFromString`, but prints nothing and returns every collected LoaderWarning alongside the definition (issue #169), and the `input_map` paths not checked (fix 1, unit 1). |
| [`AuthGithub`](#authgithub) | interface | GitHub HMAC-SHA256 hex body signature (header 'X-Hub-Signature-256'). |
| [`AuthHmac`](#authhmac) | interface | Generic HMAC body signature with a configurable header / algorithm / encoding. |
| [`AuthNone`](#authnone) | interface | Documented, discouraged escape hatch — accept without verification (trusted network / localhost only). |
| [`AuthSharedSecret`](#authsharedsecret) | interface | Header-token auth — the request carries a user-configured header equal to a shared secret. |
| [`AuthStripe`](#authstripe) | interface | Stripe timestamped HMAC body signature (header 'Stripe-Signature'). |
| [`DeclaredNames`](#declarednames) | interface | The handler and adapter names the project's realm.yaml declares, built or not. |
| [`DedupConfig`](#dedupconfig) | interface | How a webhook trigger drops a repeated event: the dot-path to the event's id, how long an id is remembered, and what to do when the id cannot be read (`WebhookTrigger.dedup`). |
| [`GateConfig`](#gateconfig) | interface | Gate configuration — choices available to the human reviewer, plus (issue #291) the authored enforce clock (`timeout_seconds`/`on_expiry`/`default_choice`) and the authored notify clock (`reminder_seconds`/`reminder_max`). |
| [`JsonSchema`](#jsonschema) | interface | The JSON Schema object a workflow gives for a step's input and for a run's params (`StepDefinition.input_schema`, `WorkflowDefinition.params_schema`). |
| [`McpServerConfig`](#mcpserverconfig) | interface | An MCP server a workflow's tool-enabled steps may call: its id and the command that starts it (`WorkflowDefinition.mcp_servers`). |
| [`NotCheckedPath`](#notcheckedpath) | interface | An `input_map` path or a `when` condition that reads data the workflow declares no shape for (`validate --json`'s `not_checked`). |
| [`ProtocolConfig`](#protocolconfig) | interface | A workflow's own words for the agent protocol: a quick-start paragraph that replaces the generated one, and rules added as they are written (`WorkflowDefinition.protocol`). |
| [`RetryConfig`](#retryconfig) | interface | How a step is tried again after a failure: the most attempts, the backoff and its delays (`StepDefinition.retry`). |
| [`ServiceDefinition`](#servicedefinition) | interface | A service a workflow declares under `services`: the adapter that calls it, its trust, and its rate limit (`WorkflowDefinition.services`). |
| [`StepDefinition`](#stepdefinition) | interface | One step of a workflow, as the loaders return it under `WorkflowDefinition.steps`: what it does, how it runs, the steps it waits for, and its input and settings. |
| [`TemplateDefinition`](#templatedefinition) | interface | A named reusable step group with parameter placeholders. |
| [`TemplateParam`](#templateparam) | interface | A single parameter declaration in a template. |
| [`TriggerFilter`](#triggerfilter) | interface | Post-normalisation form (loader converts shorthand → { all: [...] }). |
| [`WebhookTrigger`](#webhooktrigger) | interface | A workflow's webhook trigger: the path it answers, how it checks requests, which requests it takes, how it drops repeats, and how it maps a payload to run params. |
| [`WorkflowContextEntry`](#workflowcontextentry) | interface | A single named entry in the workflow_context section. |
| [`WorkflowDefinition`](#workflowdefinition) | interface | A workflow as the loaders return it: its id, name and version, its params schema, its steps, and its services, protocol and trigger when it has them. |
| [`ContextWrapperFormat`](#contextwrapperformat) | type | Wrapper format applied to {{ workflow.context.NAME }} template references. |
| [`ErrorCode`](#errorcode) | type | Every code a `WorkflowError` can carry, grouped by its category; a reply's error and the error catalogue name it (`WorkflowError.code`). |
| [`ExecutionMode`](#executionmode) | type | The kinds of step a workflow declares in `execution`: `auto`, `agent`, `guard` and `finalizer` (`StepDefinition.execution`). |
| [`FilterCondition`](#filtercondition) | type | One condition of a webhook trigger's filter: a header or a dot-path into the payload, and the value it must equal or the values one of which it must equal; a request that fails a condition is ignored. |
| [`FinalizerTrigger`](#finalizertrigger) | type | Terminal outcome(s) a finalizer step matches. |
| [`InputMapNode`](#inputmapnode) | type | One node of a step's `input_map`: a dot-path string, a `$literal` value, or an object of further nodes (`StepDefinition.input_map`). |
| [`LiteralNode`](#literalnode) | type | A node in an input_map tree. |
| [`NotCheckedWhy`](#notcheckedwhy) | type | Why a path was not checked. |
| [`ServiceTrust`](#servicetrust) | type | The words a workflow's `services: <name>: trust:` takes (`ServiceDefinition.trust`). |
| [`TriggerDefinition`](#triggerdefinition) | type | What starts a workflow's runs from outside; today a webhook is the only kind (`WorkflowDefinition.trigger`). |
| [`TriggerRule`](#triggerrule) | type | Controls when a step becomes eligible based on its dependencies' outcomes. |
| [`TrustLevel`](#trustlevel) | type | The words a step's `trust` takes: `auto`, or `human_confirmed` and `human_reviewed`, which open a gate a person answers (`StepDefinition.trust`). |
| [`WebhookAuth`](#webhookauth) | type | How a webhook trigger checks that a request is genuine: a shared secret, GitHub's or Stripe's signature, an HMAC, or none (`WebhookTrigger.auth`). |

## Functions

### loadWorkflowFromFile

function · public

Loads a WorkflowDefinition from a YAML file on disk. UNCHANGED signature/return type — the
non-breaking invariant (issue #169): every existing execution caller keeps compiling and
printing warnings for free. Structured warnings are reachable only via
`loadWorkflowFromFileWithDiagnostics`.

`@throws` WorkflowError on read failure or structural validation errors.

```ts
function loadWorkflowFromFile(filePath: string, registry?: ExtensionRegistry): WorkflowDefinition;
```

### loadWorkflowFromFileWithDiagnostics

function · public

Same as `loadWorkflowFromFile`, but prints nothing and returns every collected LoaderWarning
alongside the definition (issue #169). Opt-in for callers that want to surface warnings
themselves (validate/register/watch/`--strict`) instead of the default console.warn behavior.
`notChecked` (fix 1, unit 1) lists the `input_map` paths into data the workflow declares no
shape for, which `validate` reports.

```ts
function loadWorkflowFromFileWithDiagnostics(filePath: string, registry?: ExtensionRegistry, declared?: DeclaredNames): {
    definition: WorkflowDefinition;
    warnings: LoaderWarning[];
    notChecked: NotCheckedPath[];
};
```

### loadWorkflowFromString

function · public

Loads a WorkflowDefinition from a YAML string. UNCHANGED signature/return type — the
non-breaking invariant (issue #169): every existing execution caller keeps compiling and
printing warnings for free. Structured warnings are reachable only via
`loadWorkflowFromStringWithDiagnostics`.
Validates structure and DAG dependency references.
A declared `extensions` key is a hard load error — extensions require file-based loading
(no directory context exists to resolve relative extension module paths against).

`@throws` WorkflowError on parse failure or structural validation errors.

```ts
function loadWorkflowFromString(content: string, registry?: ExtensionRegistry): WorkflowDefinition;
```

### loadWorkflowFromStringWithDiagnostics

function · public

Same as `loadWorkflowFromString`, but prints nothing and returns every collected LoaderWarning
alongside the definition (issue #169), and the `input_map` paths not checked (fix 1, unit 1).

```ts
function loadWorkflowFromStringWithDiagnostics(content: string, registry?: ExtensionRegistry, declared?: DeclaredNames): {
    definition: WorkflowDefinition;
    warnings: LoaderWarning[];
    notChecked: NotCheckedPath[];
};
```

## Interfaces

### AuthGithub

interface · public

GitHub HMAC-SHA256 hex body signature (header 'X-Hub-Signature-256').

```ts
interface AuthGithub {
    mode: 'github';
    secret_from: string;
}
```

### AuthHmac

interface · public

Generic HMAC body signature with a configurable header / algorithm / encoding.

```ts
interface AuthHmac {
    mode: 'hmac';
    secret_from: string;
    header: string;
    algorithm?: 'sha1' | 'sha256' | 'sha512';
    encoding?: 'hex' | 'base64';
    timestamp_header?: string;
    max_age_seconds?: number;
}
```

### AuthNone

interface · public

Documented, discouraged escape hatch — accept without verification (trusted network / localhost only).

```ts
interface AuthNone {
    mode: 'none';
}
```

### AuthSharedSecret

interface · public

Header-token auth — the request carries a user-configured header equal to a shared secret.

```ts
interface AuthSharedSecret {
    mode: 'shared_secret';
    header: string;
    secret_from: string;
}
```

### AuthStripe

interface · public

Stripe timestamped HMAC body signature (header 'Stripe-Signature').

```ts
interface AuthStripe {
    mode: 'stripe';
    secret_from: string;
    max_age_seconds?: number;
}
```

### DeclaredNames

interface · public

The handler and adapter names the project's realm.yaml declares, built or not.

```ts
interface DeclaredNames {
    readonly handlers?: readonly string[];
    readonly adapters?: readonly string[];
}
```

### DedupConfig

interface · public

How a webhook trigger drops a repeated event: the dot-path to the event's id, how long an id is
remembered, and what to do when the id cannot be read (`WebhookTrigger.dedup`).

```ts
interface DedupConfig {
    id_from: string;
    ttl_minutes?: number;
    on_missing_id?: 'skip' | 'reject';
}
```

### GateConfig

interface · public

Gate configuration — choices available to the human reviewer, plus (issue #291) the authored
enforce clock (`timeout_seconds`/`on_expiry`/`default_choice`) and the authored notify clock
(`reminder_seconds`/`reminder_max`). See `docs/reference/yaml-schema.md`'s `structured_output`-
adjacent `## Gate timeout` section for the full authoring/enactment/disclosure contract; the
loader (`yaml-loader.ts`) is the normative validator for every field below.

```ts
interface GateConfig {
    choices?: string[];
    owner?: string;
    answerers?: string[];
    message?: string;
    resolution_messages?: Record<string, string>;
    timeout_seconds?: number;
    on_expiry?: 'settle_default' | 'abort';
    default_choice?: string;
    reminder_seconds?: number;
    reminder_max?: number;
}
```

### JsonSchema

interface · public

The JSON Schema object a workflow gives for a step's input and for a run's params
(`StepDefinition.input_schema`, `WorkflowDefinition.params_schema`).

```ts
interface JsonSchema {
    type?: string;
    required?: string[];
    properties?: Record<string, JsonSchema>;
    items?: JsonSchema;
    minimum?: number;
    maximum?: number;
    pattern?: string;
    [key: string]: unknown;
}
```

### McpServerConfig

interface · public

An MCP server a workflow's tool-enabled steps may call: its id and the command that starts it
(`WorkflowDefinition.mcp_servers`).

```ts
interface McpServerConfig {
    id: string;
    transport: 'stdio';
    command?: string;
    args?: string[];
    env?: Record<string, string>;
}
```

### NotCheckedPath

interface · public

An `input_map` path or a `when` condition that reads data the workflow declares no shape for
(`validate --json`'s `not_checked`).

```ts
interface NotCheckedPath {
    surface: 'input_map' | 'when' | 'template';
    step: string;
    key: string;
    path: string;
    why: NotCheckedWhy | 'check_failed';
}
```

### ProtocolConfig

interface · public

A workflow's own words for the agent protocol: a quick-start paragraph that replaces the
generated one, and rules added as they are written (`WorkflowDefinition.protocol`).

```ts
interface ProtocolConfig {
    quick_start?: string;
    rules?: string[];
}
```

### RetryConfig

interface · public

How a step is tried again after a failure: the most attempts, the backoff and its delays
(`StepDefinition.retry`).

```ts
interface RetryConfig {
    max_attempts: number;
    backoff?: 'linear' | 'exponential' | 'fixed';
    base_delay_ms?: number;
    max_delay_ms?: number;
    on_timeout?: boolean;
    total_timeout_seconds?: number;
}
```

### ServiceDefinition

interface · public

A service a workflow declares under `services`: the adapter that calls it, its trust, and its
rate limit (`WorkflowDefinition.services`).

```ts
interface ServiceDefinition {
    adapter: string;
    trust: ServiceTrust;
    rate_limit?: RateLimitConfig;
}
```

### StepDefinition

interface · public

One step of a workflow, as the loaders return it under `WorkflowDefinition.steps`: what it does,
how it runs, the steps it waits for, and its input and settings.

```ts
interface StepDefinition {
    description: string;
    execution: ExecutionMode;
    depends_on?: string[];
    trigger_rule?: TriggerRule;
    when?: string | string[];
    abort_unless?: string | string[];
    abort_message?: string;
    on_outcome?: FinalizerTrigger | FinalizerTrigger[];
    idempotent?: boolean;
    uses_service?: string;
    service_method?: 'fetch' | 'create' | 'update' | 'delete';
    operation?: string;
    input_map?: Record<string, InputMapNode>;
    handler?: string;
    config?: Record<string, unknown>;
    input_schema?: JsonSchema;
    output_schema?: JsonSchema;
    trace_schema?: JsonSchema;
    trace_validation_mode?: 'warn' | 'enforce';
    preconditions?: string[];
    trust?: TrustLevel;
    llm_timeout_seconds?: number;
    timeout_seconds?: number;
    retry?: RetryConfig;
    validation_exhaustion?: {
        threshold?: number;
        mode?: 'fail' | 'default';
        default_output?: unknown;
    };
    instructions?: string;
    prompt?: string;
    display?: string;
    use_template?: string;
    gate?: GateConfig;
    agent_profile?: string;
    tools?: string[];
    max_tool_calls?: number;
    max_fan_out?: number;
    tool_timeout?: number;
    structured_output?: 'strict';
}
```

### TemplateDefinition

interface · public

A named reusable step group with parameter placeholders.

```ts
interface TemplateDefinition {
    params?: Record<string, TemplateParam>;
    steps: Record<string, StepDefinition>;
}
```

### TemplateParam

interface · public

A single parameter declaration in a template.

```ts
interface TemplateParam {
    required?: boolean;
    default?: string;
}
```

### TriggerFilter

interface · public

Post-normalisation form (loader converts shorthand → { all: [...] }). Max 8 conditions.

```ts
interface TriggerFilter {
    all: FilterCondition[];
}
```

### WebhookTrigger

interface · public

A workflow's webhook trigger: the path it answers, how it checks requests, which requests it
takes, how it drops repeats, and how it maps a payload to run params.

```ts
interface WebhookTrigger {
    type: 'webhook';
    path?: string;
    auth: WebhookAuth;
    filter?: TriggerFilter;
    dedup?: DedupConfig | false;
    params_map?: Record<string, string>;
    result_map?: Record<string, string>;
}
```

### WorkflowContextEntry

interface · public

A single named entry in the workflow_context section.

```ts
interface WorkflowContextEntry {
    source: {
        path: string;
    };
    description?: string;
}
```

### WorkflowDefinition

interface · public

A workflow as the loaders return it: its id, name and version, its params schema, its steps, and
its services, protocol and trigger when it has them.

```ts
interface WorkflowDefinition {
    id: string;
    name: string;
    description?: string;
    version: number;
    params_schema?: JsonSchema;
    protocol?: ProtocolConfig;
    services?: Record<string, ServiceDefinition>;
    mcp_servers?: McpServerConfig[];
    templates?: Record<string, TemplateDefinition>;
    steps: Record<string, StepDefinition>;
    profiles_dir?: string;
    extensions?: string | string[];
    source_dir?: string;
    trust_root?: string;
    resolved_profiles?: Record<string, {
        content: string;
        content_hash: string;
    }>;
    schema_version?: number;
    workflow_context?: Record<string, WorkflowContextEntry>;
    context_wrapper?: ContextWrapperFormat;
    origin?: 'human' | 'agent';
    model?: string;
    agent?: string;
    trigger?: TriggerDefinition;
}
```

### ExecutionMode

type · public

The kinds of step a workflow declares in `execution`: `auto`, `agent`, `guard` and `finalizer`
(`StepDefinition.execution`).

```ts
type ExecutionMode = 'auto' | 'agent' | 'guard' | 'finalizer';
```

### FilterCondition

type · public

One condition of a webhook trigger's filter: a header or a dot-path into the payload, and the
value it must equal or the values one of which it must equal; a request that fails a condition is
ignored.

```ts
type FilterCondition = {
    header: string;
    value: string | string[];
} | {
    path: string;
    value: string | string[];
};
```

### FinalizerTrigger

type · public

Terminal outcome(s) a finalizer step matches. `execution: finalizer` steps run at the
run's terminal transition (a workflow-level try/catch/finally): `complete` = success,
`fail`/`abort` = catch, `always` = finally, `completed_with_failed_steps` = a `complete`
seal that still carries `failed_steps` (issue #302 — author-opt-in; fires IN ADDITION to
`complete`/`always` on that specific seal shape; never fires on a clean complete or on a pure
fail/abort seal — see `docs/reference/yaml-schema.md`'s `execution: finalizer` trigger table).
OR-membership when given as an array.

```ts
type FinalizerTrigger = 'complete' | 'fail' | 'abort' | 'always' | 'completed_with_failed_steps';
```

### InputMapNode

type · public

One node of a step's `input_map`: a dot-path string, a `$literal` value, or an object of further
nodes (`StepDefinition.input_map`).

```ts
type InputMapNode = string | LiteralNode | {
    [key: string]: InputMapNode;
};
```

### LiteralNode

type · public

A node in an input_map tree. One of:
- string: a dot-path reference resolved against run state
- { $literal: value }: a static constant value (any JSON value: scalar, array, or object) —
  passed through verbatim by the runtime, never path-resolved or recursed into
- { [key: string]: InputMapNode }: a nested object (recursive)

The $literal sentinel must appear alone — no sibling keys are permitted.

```ts
type LiteralNode = {
    $literal: unknown;
};
```

### NotCheckedWhy

type · public

Why a path was not checked. Piece 3a-ii-a: `added_from_file` is `workflow.context.schema`, an entry
the file loader adds from a `schema.json` beside the file when the workflow declares none.

```ts
type NotCheckedWhy = 'producer_declares_no_shape' | 'no_params_schema' | 'added_from_file';
```

### ServiceTrust

type · public

The words a workflow's `services: <name>: trust:` takes (`ServiceDefinition.trust`).

```ts
type ServiceTrust = 'engine_delivered' | 'engine_managed' | 'agent_provided';
```

### TriggerDefinition

type · public

What starts a workflow's runs from outside; today a webhook is the only kind
(`WorkflowDefinition.trigger`).

```ts
type TriggerDefinition = WebhookTrigger;
```

### TriggerRule

type · public

Controls when a step becomes eligible based on its dependencies' outcomes.
Default: 'all_success'.

```ts
type TriggerRule = 'all_success' | 'all_failed' | 'all_done' | 'one_failed' | 'one_success' | 'none_failed';
```

### TrustLevel

type · public

The words a step's `trust` takes: `auto`, or `human_confirmed` and `human_reviewed`, which open
a gate a person answers (`StepDefinition.trust`).

```ts
type TrustLevel = 'auto' | 'human_confirmed' | 'human_reviewed';
```

### WebhookAuth

type · public

How a webhook trigger checks that a request is genuine: a shared secret, GitHub's or Stripe's
signature, an HMAC, or none (`WebhookTrigger.auth`).

```ts
type WebhookAuth = AuthSharedSecret | AuthGithub | AuthStripe | AuthHmac | AuthNone;
```

## Also used by this job

Names this job reaches whose entry is on another page.

- [`AbandonWay`](write-a-handler.md#abandonway): End the run.
- [`AdvanceWay`](write-a-handler.md#advanceway): Have the engine carry out what it owes (#625 PR-2a's act): a due expiry first, then steps.
- [`AgentAction`](write-a-handler.md#agentaction): What an agent does next (engine-owned, R3).
- [`AnswererMismatchFacts`](write-a-handler.md#answerermismatchfacts): #603 A3a: an answer refused because its sender is not one the question lets answer — the names that may (as written: the question's `owner` and `answerers`, or the project's list), and the account the channel reported for the sender.
- [`Base`](write-a-handler.md#base): What every way carries: its verb and the conditions it is offered with; each way type adds its own fields to it.
- [`Cond`](write-a-handler.md#cond): A condition a way is offered with (PR0-CONTRACT §1, D2 D-4): offered with condition c, it is admitted only when c is met (D3 A-4).
- [`COND_TAGS`](write-a-handler.md#cond_tags): #627 W: who discharges a condition outside Realm (`client`: the MCP client's own approval prompt).
- [`CondTag`](write-a-handler.md#condtag): Who discharges a condition outside Realm; `client` is the MCP client's own approval prompt (`Cond`'s `client_prompt` member).
- [`DueExpiry`](write-a-handler.md#dueexpiry): An open question whose time is up and whose `on_expiry` the engine can carry out (decision C95).
- [`ErrorCategory`](write-a-handler.md#errorcategory): The broad kind of failure a `WorkflowError` reports: network, an outside service, the run's state, invalid input, the engine itself, or a resource (`WorkflowError.category`).
- [`ErrorFacts`](write-a-handler.md#errorfacts): Any typed error facts.
- [`ErrorFactsByCode`](write-a-handler.md#errorfactsbycode): The error codes whose facts are typed (PR0-CONTRACT Amendments 7, 11): ONE facts type per code, entering with the unit that types it.
- [`ExtensionIdentityEntry`](write-a-handler.md#extensionidentityentry): One point-in-time identity of the extension code executing a run.
- [`ExtensionIdentityModule`](write-a-handler.md#extensionidentitymodule): One loaded extension module's identity.
- [`ExtensionIdentitySignals`](write-a-handler.md#extensionidentitysignals): Labeled advisory signals — each independently fail-soft; never part of the comparison.
- [`ExtensionIdentityTree`](write-a-handler.md#extensionidentitytree): Versioned deterministic directory-tree fingerprint over the module roots.
- [`ExtensionRegistry`](run-and-drive-a-run.md#extensionregistry): The handlers, service adapters and processors a program registers by name; the engine looks a step's handler or adapter up in it.
- [`InspectWay`](write-a-handler.md#inspectway): Read the run's record.
- [`LoaderWarning`](write-a-handler.md#loaderwarning): A single structured diagnostic.
- [`NewerDefinitionFacts`](write-a-handler.md#newerdefinitionfacts): #627 W (W-r2; MA 3's decision 2026-10-16, Amendment 11's rule — a code's facts enter with its owner): a registered workflow's copy written by a LATER Realm — the copy's path, the definition format it states, and the latest this version reads.
- [`PresentWay`](write-a-handler.md#presentway): #627 W (Amendment 2): show the open question again, as a form in the agent's own call — the MCP door's `present_question`.
- [`Processor`](write-a-handler.md#processor): A program's step that changes content, registered under its `id` and run in order by `runPipeline`.
- [`ProcessorInput`](write-a-handler.md#processorinput): The text and metadata a processor is given (`Processor.process`).
- [`ProcessorOutput`](write-a-handler.md#processoroutput): The text and metadata a processor returns; the next processor in the pipeline is given it.
- [`RateLimitConfig`](write-a-handler.md#ratelimitconfig): How fast Realm calls a service: requests per second, the burst it allows, and how long it waits after a 429 (`ServiceDefinition.rate_limit`).
- [`RateLimiter`](write-a-handler.md#ratelimiter): Controls the rate at which requests are sent to an external service.
- [`ReclaimWay`](write-a-handler.md#reclaimway): #922 (D3 §4): free a held step so it can run again — a person's act, never an agent's.
- [`RegisterWay`](write-a-handler.md#registerway): Register the run's workflow again (D3 A-10): no JUDGE — on MCP an elsewhere entry.
- [`RespondWay`](write-a-handler.md#respondway): Answer the run's open question (PR0-CONTRACT §1).
- [`RunRecordFieldProblem`](write-a-handler.md#runrecordfieldproblem): One field a value lacks, or holds with the wrong type.
- [`RunStepWay`](write-a-handler.md#runstepway): Run one step: an agent step's answer, or (the operator's lever, T-17) an engine step's input.
- [`ServiceAdapter`](write-a-handler.md#serviceadapter): Service adapter — handles communication with a specific external API.
- [`ServiceResponse`](write-a-handler.md#serviceresponse): What a service adapter's call returns: the HTTP status and the data (`ServiceAdapter`'s methods).
- [`SIDE_FILE_KINDS`](write-a-handler.md#side_file_kinds): issue #719 (F4): the kinds of side file a run keeps beside its file, in its runs folder — exported by name as one const and its type (#729 PR-0, PR0-CONTRACT Amendment 7d).
- [`SideFileKind`](write-a-handler.md#sidefilekind): One of `SIDE_FILE_KINDS`.
- [`Slot`](write-a-handler.md#slot): A value the caller picks from a closed set (D1 spine 1): printed by each door's own rule (T-7).
- [`StableBoundary`](write-a-handler.md#stableboundary): Caching 3-B (C1): where a rendered text stops repeating between runs, in UTF-16 code units.
- [`StepBrief`](write-a-handler.md#stepbrief): What a `run_step` way says about its step (D1 spine 3, 4): the step's kind, its description, the prompt the agent reads (template-resolved), the input schema an agent step's answer must fit, and — a fact kept as data until #516 decides its meaning — the step's handler.
- [`StepContext`](write-a-handler.md#stepcontext): What a handler is told about the run: its id and params, the step's `config`, and earlier steps' outputs in `resources`, keyed by step id (`StepHandler.execute`'s second argument).
- [`StepHandler`](write-a-handler.md#stephandler): A program's code for an `auto` step named by `handler:`: registered under its `id`, and called with the step's input and the run's context.
- [`StepHandlerInputs`](write-a-handler.md#stephandlerinputs): What a handler is given as input: the step's params, after its `input_map` when it has one (`StepHandler.execute`'s first argument).
- [`StepHandlerResult`](write-a-handler.md#stephandlerresult): What a handler returns: the step's output, and optionally a state update, a clean abort or a warning (`StepHandler.execute`'s result).
- [`STORED_FILE_CLASSES`](write-a-handler.md#stored_file_classes): What a damaged stored JSON file is (issue #719, R7) — the shipped vocabulary of the registrar's listing, plus the run-only classes: - `empty`: zero bytes, or whitespace only; - `parse`: not JSON, or JSON that is not an object (`shape` says what it is); - `not_a_run`: an object that is not a run record (`fields` names what is missing or mistyped); - `mismatched`: a run record whose `id` is not the file's name (`held_id`, `held_file`); - `legacy`: written by an earlier Realm (`state` without `completed_steps`); - `unreadable`: the file (or the runs folder) cannot be read (`errno`).
- [`StoredFileClass`](write-a-handler.md#storedfileclass): What is wrong with a damaged stored file: empty, not JSON, not a run, filed under another id, from an earlier Realm, or unreadable (`UnreadableFileFacts.class`).
- [`StoredFileErrorFacts`](write-a-handler.md#storedfileerrorfacts): The typed facts of a damaged stored file's error (issue #729 PR-0, PR0-CONTRACT Amendments 7, 7b, 7e): one file (`scope: 'file'`, #719's `UnreadableFileFacts`) or a decision over every run that failed closed (`scope: 'files'`, `UnreadableRunFilesFacts`).
- [`UnreadableFileFacts`](run-and-drive-a-run.md#unreadablefilefacts): The facts of one damaged stored file (issue #719, R7; #729 PR-0 Amendments 7, 7e): names, classes and type words — never its content.
- [`UnreadableRunFilesFacts`](write-a-handler.md#unreadablerunfilesfacts): What `unreadableRunFilesError` carries: the command that did not run, the runs folder, and every run file it could not read.
- [`ValidationErrorFacts`](write-a-handler.md#validationerrorfacts): issue #759 (PR0-CONTRACT Amendment 11 — its first owner of the validation codes): the typed facts of a refused answer — the validator's rows (`errors`, Ajv's own order, capped at `VALIDATION_PROBLEMS_SHOWN`, never re-sorted or de-duplicated), the total before the cap (`error_count`, counted once at the validator and carried — never recounted by a renderer), and, for an agent step's counted rejection, the countdown (`rejections`, `threshold`).
- [`WarningCode`](write-a-handler.md#warningcode): Every warning code the workflow loader can give (`LoaderWarning.code`).
- [`WAY_VERBS`](write-a-handler.md#way_verbs): PR-0's verbs (option B) and #627 W's `present` (Amendment 2): PR-1 adds resume/drain/purge, PR-2 reclaim/validate/export, PR-7 start.
- [`WayOn`](write-a-handler.md#wayon): One way on, discriminated on `verb` (PR0-CONTRACT §1).
- [`WayVerb`](write-a-handler.md#wayverb): The acts a way names: answer a question, run a step, have the engine carry out what it owes, read the run, end it, register its workflow again, or send a question's form to the person (`Base.verb`).
- [`WorkflowCopyFault`](write-a-handler.md#workflowcopyfault): What a registered copy that is a JSON object lacks to be a workflow (#627 W correction 2; #819 U2 `no_steps`, U3 `not_legacy_shape`).
- [`WorkflowError`](write-a-handler.md#workflowerror): The error Realm throws and records, carrying a code, a category and what the agent does next; a handler throws one with `retryable: true` to have its step tried again when the step has a `retry` block.
- [`WorkflowErrorOptions`](write-a-handler.md#workflowerroroptions): What a `WorkflowError` is built with: its code and category, what the agent does next, whether it may be tried again, and the optional facts, step and ways on.
